This further improves traversal speed by identifying pixels with no intersections [S1].

The claim states that identifying pixels with no intersections improves traversal speed. The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly states: 'This optimization frequently allows us to find pixels whose entire beams have no intersection with geometry, and for these pixels, no additional shadow rays are required.' It also states just before this: 'By simply tracing the same beam rays in the reverse direction... This improves traversal speed of the shadow rays further.' The combination of these statements confirms that finding pixels with no intersections (and thus skipping further ray casting for them) is the mechanism by which traversal speed is improved.
